full_judgment:
2. Short facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule, are that 59 decimals of land appertaining to SA Plot No. 209 under SA khatian No. 113, JL No. 323, Lamashempur, Gowainghat, Sylhet belonged to the predecessors of the SA recorded tenant Mosrab Ali who orally gifted the said land to the petitioner Lamashempur Jame Mosque of whose Motwalli is Hafiz Nazrul Islam, successor of Mosrab Ali. The Mosque Committee has been possessing the land by constructing a Mosque thereon and connecting electricity line and paying electricity bill regularly on behalf of the said mosque. But the draft RoR was prepared neither in the name of the petitioner nor in the name of the respondent No. 4. The respondent No. 4, Lamashempur Purbotul Jame Mosque represented by Motwalli Abdul Musabbir filed Objection Case No. 399 before the Settlement Officer under rule 30 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 which was allowed on 27-4-2009 in absence of the petitioner and draft record-of-right was prepared in the name of the respondent No. 4, Lamashempur Purbotull Jame Mosque. 

 5. Mr Khairul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque is the owner and possessor of the land in dispute which was not recorded in the draft khatian in the name of petitioner for which the petitioner filed an appeal being No. 13274 of 2015 under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and obtained an order on contest. He also submits that where there is no specific allegation of fraud in the elements of fraud in the whole proceeding, no question of review lies since the settlement authority has got no jurisdiction to reopen the matter other than to send the draft publication khatian for final publication under rule 32 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and even the said rule 42A does not empower the Settlement Officer to sit and act as an appellate authority over an appellate order passed under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and, as such, the petition filed under rule 42A is not entertainable rather it is liable to be rejected. He relied upon the decision passed in the case of Zahirul Islam vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 65 DLR 168. 

 8. We have perused the materials on record meticulously. It appears from the record that the respondent No. 4 appeared in the appeal filed under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. It also appears that the appeal being No. 13274 of 2015 was disposed of in presence of the respondent No. 4 who claimed that there is no existence of Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque. But it appears from the findings of the Appeal Officer passed in appeal No. 13274 of 2015 that the Motwalli of respondent No. 4 namely Musabbir was present in a meeting held by the petitioner Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque on 14-6-2016 and put his signature on the resolution sheet in serial No. 1. In that meeting it was decided that for the development of Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque, a portion of land to be sold out. Accordingly a sale deed was prepared whereon the Motwalli of respondent No. 4 Musabbir put his signature and thus the respondent No. 4 admitted the existence of the petitioner Lamashempur A timer Jame Mosque. Moreover, it appears from the findings of the Appeal Officer that there are four separate undisputed DP khatian Nos. 260, 146, 327 and 506 were prepared in the name of the petitioner Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque which support the existence of the Lamashempur Jame Mosque. Thereafter, the Appeal Officer decided that there is existence of Lamashempur Jame Mosque. His finding is well reasoned, we find nothing to disbelieve the same. 

 12. It appears from the application filed under rule 42A that the respondent No. 4 did not challenge the findings of the Appeal Officer as to existence of the Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque and his signature put on the resolution sheet and sale deed as stated in the findings passed in the appeal under rule 31. The application filed under rule 42A contains no specific allegation of fraud. Respondent No. 4 stated in the application under rule 42A that the Appeal Officer admitted the appeal on 25-11-2015 illegally after 6 years and 5 months from the disposal of the Objection Case No. 399 on 27-4-2009 and he illegally condoned 6 years 5 months delay and, as such, committed fraud. But, on perusal of the record it appears that the DP khatian was prepared neither in the name of the petitioner nor in the name of the respondent No. 4. The respondent No. 4 filed Objection Case No. 399 and obtained order in his favour. Admittedly in that objection case the petitioner Lamashempur Atimer Jame Mosque was not party. Subsequently, the petitioner came to know about the objection case and filed an appeal under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. It also appears that considering the facts and circumstances the Appeal Officer condoned the period of Limitation. We are of the view that the Appeal Officer is fully authorized by law to condone delay in filing the appeal if the facts and circumstances permit him. On perusal of the materials on record it reveals that the Appeal Officer rightly condoned the delay considering the existing facts and circumstances of the case. So, condonation of delay in filing of the appeal cannot be considered as fraud. It is settled principle of law that a mere allegation of fraud is not sufficient unless the ingredients of fraud are disclosed in the petition for taking cognizance of allegation. Hence, we are of the view that ingredients of fraud was not detected or disclosed in the petition filed by the respondent No. 4 under rule 42A or proceedings under rules 28-31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 14. We have gone through the facts and-decisions of both the cases. It appears from the case of Mainuddin Ahmed vs Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh and others reported in 7 SCOB (2016) 134 that two Settlement Appeals being Nos. 8970 of 2003 and 11915 of 2008 were filed under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. Settlement Appeal No. 8970 of 2003 was dismissed on contest, but settlement Appeal No. 11915 of 2008 was dismissed in absence of the appellant. The High Court Division stated in the judgment that the Appeal Officer committed a serious error in disposing the settlement appeal No. 11915 of 2008 in absence of the appellant and on 20-8-2009 respondent No. 12 submitted an application to the respondent No. 3 with a complaint of fraudulent entry in the DP khatian as to case property upon stating the fact of his absence at the time of disposal of the said settlement appeal No. 11915 of 2008. On the basis of that allegation respondent No. 3 directed respondent No 5 to submit a report upon carrying out a preliminary investigation under rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. Having been, thus asked by a superior authority respondent No. 5 conducted an inquiry into the allegation of committing fraud and submitted an elaborate report to respondent No. 3. Through the said investigation, it was revealed that the opponent of the settlement appeal No. 8970 of 2003 and the settlement appeal No. 11915 of 2009 (Mainuddin Ahmed) do not have any physical possession in the property and, thus, the said investigation hinted at the existence of prima-facie elements of fraud. Thereafter the respondent No. 3 settlement officer issued notice under rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. So, it appears that after detection of existence of prima facie elements of fraud in the aforesaid case, the Settlement Officer has issued notice under rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 18. In that case it has been decided that once appeal has been disposed of on contest under rule 31 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 no review (.....) lies and the settlement authorities have got no jurisdiction to reopen the matter other than to send the draft publication khatian for final publication under rule 32 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955.
